label: no
controls_available: Click one of the three visible ingredient jars to load or replace an ingredient.
Click one of five discrete curve-notch buttons to choose the grind step.
Click STIR PATH repeatedly; each click advances the prepared path synchronously by six of its 24 samples and the final click commits that ingredient path.
Click WATER when the mortar is empty; each use moves synchronously toward the origin by up to 40 px, with a budget of 7.
Click BELLOWS when the mortar is empty; each use moves synchronously along the current heading by 22 px, with a budget of 6.
Click SEAL to submit the current effect; this is administrative certification rather than an outcome-affecting run action.
The declared mouse and keyboard action surfaces are available, but the simplified mechanic installs no outcome-affecting keyboard control.

autonomous_processes.period: Between all outcome-affecting clicks during the active simplified run
autonomous_processes.changes: None to the task state: selected ingredient, notch, position, route progress, budgets, hazard contacts, vortices, and revealed trace change only inside click handlers.
A 1.8-second timeout only removes the fresh-failure presentation overlay and restores the idle readout; it does not evolve the map state or an action opportunity.
The runner clock may advance, but no simplified-mode timer, animation callback, or physics process changes the outcome state.

grouped_control_modes.note: Administrative submission; not a candidate outcome-affecting D for the pre-run rule.

clause_i.reason: For a candidate D such as curve-notch selection after an ingredient is loaded, the generator varies ingredient geometry and route gates across seeds while the same prior jar/notch action history can recur. The visible gate and path preview determine the correct notch, so no policy using only I_t can be uniformly optimal.

clause_ii.reason: For that same visual-decision mode, the current screenshot exposes the selected jar, curve preview, and visible route ring with its center aperture and heading fan; one endpoint frame within the configured 240 ms bound is sufficient to choose the action. This is ordinary static visual grounding, not evidence of a changing post-delay state.

clause_iii.reason: No valid Delta can witness strict loss. In simplified mode the jar, notch, stir, water, and bellows handlers update the model synchronously, and full-only duration grinding is rejected. During an idle delay H_t^tau is outcome-equivalent to H_t, so an available action's Q and Q-minus-no-op value do not strictly decrease. The sole 1.8-second timeout only clears a failure overlay.

common_visible_process: None. The only candidate autonomous change is failure-overlay cleanup after an unsuccessful seal; it is administrative presentation state, not a visible task-state process that degrades an outcome-affecting action. Therefore clauses (i) and (ii) cannot be paired with clause (iii) under one D, Delta, and w.

pre_run.reason: The exact simplified mechanic has no autonomous outcome phase. Every successful generated instance requires post-preparation outcome-affecting jar/notch/stir and, when needed, recovery clicks before the administrative seal; the only no-action timeout is presentation cleanup. Thus the defined pre-run solution is not available for at least half of instances. The mathematical failure of clause (iii) already fixes the catalog label as No.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 is the three-ingredient, two-route, five-notch, no-vortex profile with 104-122 px paths, 38-58 degree curves, seven water uses, six bellows uses, and one tolerated bone contact.
Simplified interaction is jar selection plus discrete curve-notch buttons; the configured observation window is 240 ms with one frame and 180 seconds of play time.
Controlled difficulty, interaction, and time-mode parameters are copied into _control_condition before generation.
The generator uses the control condition's difficulty_parameters instead of the baseline when a controlled configuration is supplied.
World geometry and solution routes are randomized from the seed and exact parameters, so route choices vary across generated instances.
The generated mechanic fixes path samples, synchronous stir stride, route feedback, interaction geometry, and the selected interaction condition in public and hidden state.
Interface state and controls are updated synchronously; simplified notch buttons are enabled only while an ingredient is selected and no path is committed.
Duration-based grinding and requestAnimationFrame progression are explicitly guarded by interaction === full.
Stir, water, and bellows mutate position, route progress, recovery budgets, and reveal state directly inside click handlers.
Simplified controls are click listeners, while the only timer is the 1.8-second fresh-failure overlay cleanup.
The pestle animation is conditional on data-grinding=true, and simplified mode disables the pestle.
The verifier replays ingredient loading, simplified grind_set, and stir events from their submitted event sequence; there is no elapsed-time or autonomous-state input.
Water, bellows, and seal are checked as explicit submitted events against synchronous replayed geometry.
Passing depends on the final replayed outcome, route progress, one seal, budgets, and hazard limits, not on timing.
The task verifier loads the exported result and invokes the independent replay grader.
The solver uses a jar click and notch-button click in simplified mode, then repeats STIR PATH clicks to advance each path.
The frozen definition requires autonomous visible state evolution and strict loss of action value inside Delta, with one common D, Delta, and w.
The pre-run rule concerns an autonomous outcome phase, and persistent actionability without task-state change does not satisfy clause (iii).
